html:
Physics Simulations

Every physics simulation in the project — mostly the Star Field engine, plus the spring/tween models used on the site — with the math each one actually runs. All constants live in core/tokens/starfield/params/*; the code below names the token that owns each number.

Parent index: animations/README.md.

1. Coordinate frames and distance compression

engine/scale.ts + engine/catalog/geo.ts.

Twenty orders of magnitude separate Neptune's orbit from the observable-universe boundary, so no linear scale can draw the cosmos. Distances compress in three continuous tiers — directions stay astronomically true, only radii compress:

flowchart LR A["galactic coords (l, b, d_ly)"] --> B["gpos()"] B --> C{"d_ly"} C -->|"d ≤ 1 Mly"| D["galactic tier<br/>1 u = 100 ly"] C -->|"1 Mly < d ≤ 10 Mly"| E["local-group tier<br/>1 u = 800 ly"] C -->|"d > 10 Mly"| F["cosmic tier<br/>1 u = 20 000 ly"] D & E & F --> G["chart units — piecewise-continuous"]

sfChartDist(ly) is piecewise-linear and continuous at both breaks (1 Mly → 10 000 units from either side), so ratios stay honest inside a tier. Solar-system bodies get an extra shrinkSolar factor so AU-scale orbits fit inside a 1 unit = 100 ly chart.

2. Keplerian orbits

engine/frame.ts — the main per-node loop.

Each orbiting body owns a pivot at the parent's center; the body sits orbit units along the pivot's local +X.

pivot.rotation.y(t) = phase + t · ORBIT_SPEED · speed
  • phase seeds the mean anomaly so siblings never start in a line.
  • speed ranks by real period (TRAPPIST-1b..h span 2.6 → 0.35).
  • inc tilts the whole pivot — the orbital plane, not the body.

Eccentricity — the conic equation

Uniform angular sweep (a stylized chart, not an N-body integrator), but the radial distance follows the true polar conic:

r(θ) = a (1 − e²) / (1 + e·cos θ),   θ = pivot.rotation.y − phase

Periapsis lands exactly on the authored phase direction; Halley-class bodies visibly plunge and coast. The radius is written on node.center (the orbit-offset carrier), not node.mesh — a mesh inside an axis-lock group would have a position write rotated away.

flowchart TB T["θ(t) = phase + t·ORBIT_SPEED·speed"] --> R["r(θ) = a(1−e²)/(1+e·cosθ)"] R --> P["center.position.x = r(θ)"] T --> A["lock.rotation.y = −θ"]

Inertial axis lock

A tilted body whose spin axis is parented under the orbit pivot would precess once per year. node.lock counter-rotates:

lock.rotation.y = −pivot.rotation.y

so the axis stays inertially fixed — the terminator sweeps hemispheres over the year, which is what makes cycle (§7) physically meaningful.

3. Axial spin + differential rotation

spinner.rotation.y(t) = t · SPIN_SPEED · spin
rotor.rotation.y(t)   = t · SPIN_SPEED · spin · ROTOR_DIFF   (galaxies)

ROTOR_DIFF = 1.6 — a volumetric galaxy's inner-disc rotor out-spins the rigid rim, the chart's honest read of a flat rotation curve (inner material should lap the outer arms, not co-rotate rigidly like a vinyl record).

4. Solar-wind activity signal

engine/frame/fx.ts → solarWindAt(t) — one shared signal every wind-touched system reads.

W(t) = BASE + WAVE_AMP·(½ + ½·sin(2πt/WAVE_PERIOD))
     + STORM_GAIN·max(0, sin(f₁·t)·sin(f₂·t + 1.3))^STORM_POW
  • BASE + WAVE — the ~11-year activity cycle compressed to scene seconds; a bounded 0.5–1 swell.
  • Storm spike — the product of two detuned sines raised to a high power: rarely positive, briefly large → sharp gusts that ignite auroras and stretch flares. Detuning matters: equal frequencies would spike on a metronome; incommensurate ones cluster and skip irregularly, like real weather.
flowchart LR S1["sin(f₁t)"] --> M["×"] S2["sin(f₂t+1.3)"] --> M M --> P["max(0,·)^POW"] P --> G["× STORM_GAIN"] W["sin(2πt/PERIOD)"] --> A["+"] G --> A A --> O["solarWind uniform"]

5. Stellar pulsation

def.pulse = { period, amp } — variable stars breathe:

k(t) = 1 + amp·sin(2πt/period)
mesh.scale = k

Betelgeuse runs period 4.2, amp 0.06 — a slow, shallow semi-regular swell, matching its real ~400-day variability.

6. Nebula layered gas dynamics

engine/bodies/deep-sky.ts + frame/fx.ts — nebulae are three stacked sprites: photo/gas base, counter-rotating echo, wide underlay glow. Each layer carries a rate derived from lcg(seedFrom('id:nebula')), so every nebula churns at its own pace:

layer.rotation(t) = layer.phase + t · layer.rate        (echo rate < 0)
layer.opacity(t)  = opBase·(1−W) + opBase·W·(½+½·sin(t·OP_FREQ + 3·phase))
sprite.scale(t)   = baseScale · (1 + BREATHE_AMP·sin(t·BREATHE_FREQ + phase))

Counter-rotation between layers reads as shear between gas at different depths; the breathing term is the cloud swelling under pressure waves.

flowchart TB subgraph sprite["one nebula = stacked sprites"] U["underlay — wide, faint, ×UNDER_RATE"] B["base — photo/seeded gas, ×rate"] E["echo — counter-rotates −rate·ECHO_RATE"] end U -->|"rotation+opacity+scale"| R["living composite"] B --> R E --> R

7. Climate cycles (Milankovitch-style)

def.cycle = { period } — glaciation tint:

  • Axis-locked bodies: k = ½ + ½·cos(pivot.rotation.y) — warm peaks at northern summer exactly when the inertial axis tips the north pole sunward. The seasons drive the ice.
  • Unlocked bodies: free-running sine on period.

material.color lerps warm → ice — Earth's glaciation is the canonical instance.

8. Meteor impact pooling

node.meteorPool — airless bodies take strikes:

  • Schedule: next hit at t + INTERVAL·(0.4 + 1.2·rand) — Poisson-ish.
  • Placement: uniform sphere sampling — u = 2·rand−1 uniform in cos θ, a = 2π·rand, r = √(1−u²) → no pole clustering.
  • Light curve: fast rise over the first 25 % of LIFE, then a slow decay — the real impact-fireball profile.
  • Pooled sprites: fixed cap, slots recycle — zero allocation per hit.

9. Corona + limb flares

  • Corona: slow in-plane UV rotation phase + t·rate; opacity shimmer 0.55 + 0.2·sin(6·rate·t + phase) scaled by 0.7 + 0.5·wind.
  • Flares: k = max(0, sin(t·rate + phase))⁴ · (0.25 + wind) — sin⁴ makes bright narrow pulses; scale stretches MIN_SCALE + MAX_STRETCH·k, so storms throw prominences into space.

10. Fly-to camera tween

engine/fly.ts — selection glides the camera over FLY_MS (2.6 s):

easeInOutCubic(p) = 4p³                p < 0.5
                  = 1 − (−2p + 2)³/2   p ≥ 0.5

The destination re-resolves the body's live world position every frame (track()), so a moving rider-mounted anchor can't strand the camera on a stale spot. Any drag/wheel input cancels instantly — the tween never fights the user.

11. Floating origin + LOD

  • followSelected pins the followed anchor at the origin each frame, so fly-to spans only the local gap — positions never carry 40 000-unit magnitudes into float32 transforms.
  • updateLod swaps high-detail meshes in/out by camera distance; checkApproach prefetches dossier JSON + near-field detail before the body is visited — lazy load ahead of need.
  • registryBodies is an LRU map: registry stars spawn real meshes on approach/selection and evict the least-recently-touched beyond the cap — 139 k catalogued objects can't all exist at once.
sequenceDiagram participant Cam as camera participant U as updates.ts participant R as registry-body.ts participant LRU as registryBodies (LRU) Cam->>U: approach radius crossed U->>R: spawn(id) R->>LRU: touch / insert body node LRU-->>R: evict oldest beyond CAP → dispose() Note over LRU: geometry, materials,<br/>textures freed

12. Star-cloud fill (WASM worker)

engine/star-cloud.ts + fill-worker.ts — the 139 563-object HYG binary catalog is a single Points draw call. Attribute fills (position/color/size) dispatch through wasm-pool when threads+WASM exist, with a synchronous JS fill as the fallback — batch work only, never per-frame.

13. Website springs & tweens

  • Genie (core/utils/motion/genie.ts) — transform-origin scale tween timed by ANIMATION_DURATIONS; compositor-only (transform), skipped entirely under prefers-reduced-motion.
  • Scroll easing (wasm-scroll.ts) — parallax progress through spring smoothing, batched in WASM where available.
  • DrawText — stroke-dashoffset reveal; the dash schedule is a wasm-pool text-timing batch.

Where each sim executes

Sim Runs on Why
Orbits, locks, tweens Main-thread JS scene-graph transforms, O(nodes)
Wind/pulse/climate/fx Main-thread JS scalar math → uniforms/colors
Weather, aurora, day/night GPU shader uniforms per-pixel
Nebula swirl GPU sprite UV rotation per-fragment
Star-cloud / fills WASM worker threads batch buffer math
Spiral fills WASM worker threads batch point generation
